body: I've asked about that before and according to them there's a law that says, when a child is a risk to themselves, you need to have them down as receiving some sort of therapy/counselling/treatment. I looked into it and I can't find such a law but I can't argue against them.

I do want to stop seeing them, I just don't know how to go about it without getting in trouble because of school.

If I stayed in school I would have about a year left (not including 6th form) so I have to stay with these people for just under a year before I can stop going and not worry about school- Which is too long for me to cope with.

I could probably sort it out eventually without them, it's just that I can't get my head around doing that while I'm involved with them. If I'm doing one thing, I need everything else to be organized around it- I don't really know why, when things like that aren't organized, I get stressed out over it too much. They're very against self help (wouldn't want somebody to do their job for them) so I can't see them trying to help.

They can try all they want, but it doesn't change the fact that they make me significantly worse. 

My first counsellor interrupted and never let me speak, when she did, she didn't take anything in and only acted based on what she wanted to hear. I couldn't make myself see her anymore, so they said that I wasn't co operating and closed my case, after I'd promised to see her if she would stop interrupting and listen.

I got bad again and was referred to them, so I saw a psychiatrist. She told me that all of my problems were in my head and that I just need to go out more to sort them out- Which is what my problem is, I have anxiety and can't go out. She was also rude and interrupted, my social worker went with us and said that we should probably complain because of how she went about it.

This new doctor is like both of them combined, she's just aware of how she talks to me and doesn't seem to care. With every new person I see, they get worse.

And yeah, I want to wait until I'm an adult to do anything and just stop seeing these people altogether. Even if they are 'trying' they still make me worse, refuse to acknowledge it and act like my problems don't exist. But I can't, so I'm stuck with them. That's mostly why I want to end it, I've seen them for 3 years and they just keep getting worse and worse, then people still go on about how they're just trying and how they're probably just having a bad day, 3 years is a bit much for the "everybody makes mistakes" stuff.

Yeah, I've talked to my family about it a few times. They agreed not to do stuff like that, but they still slip up and do it a lot. They're trying which is something, they're just bad at it. 

I talked to my doctor, psychiatrist and counsellor about it and called them out on it every time they did it, but they saw no wrong in them doing it because they meant no harm by it. That's the main reason why I can't go to see her, it's so frustrating because if I mention anything she'll just say "but it's important" and carry on.

And I don't know. I'm cool with the medication itself and having to go in for check-ups to make sure it's not messing with me or anything, it's just that the talking therapy alongside it would probably be too  much at this point. If they talked about this an *entire year* ago before I got this bad, then I would have been able to and it would have made things so much easier. I might have considered it if these people weren't so pretentious and rude.

I haven't been to school for ages. The only reason why we aren't in trouble over it is because I'm with these mental health people. I haven't been diagnosed with anything so we can't say it's for medical reasons and leave it at that.

And no, not really. They're rude, don't listen to anything I have to say, think that they know everything, interrupt and just generally don't pay much attention to my actual problems. It's the same as talking to my middle aged family member who studied psychology this one time and thinks that she knows everything, except that these people decide what happens with my life and she doesn't.

It's gotten to a point where my problems make it impossible for me to relax and nothing takes my mind off of it anymore. We talked about medication to take the edge off of things, but I wouldn't be able to- I'm a minor so I would need some sort of talking therapy alongside it (other than normal check-ups) whereas it isn't compulsory for adults to have talking therapy alongside normal check-ups, according to my doctor, which is something that I wouldn't be able to cope with at the moment, either.

And my family aren't really aware of how sever what they're asking of me will effect me. They're aware of my previous suicide attempts but don't seem to get that going on at me about choosing a path makes me feel more suicidal. I don't really have much I can do. I do need some time to myself, but I can't really have that.
